title: Global derived Hom complex
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let D(\mathcal O_X) be its derived category of \mathcal O_X-modules [def-pc-derived-category]. Put A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X) and let p:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(\{\mathrm{pt}\},A) be the morphism of ringed spaces to the one-point space with structure ring A, with p^\sharp the identity of A=\mathcal O_X(X); modules over (\{\mathrm{pt}\},A) are A-modules, so its derived category is D(A). Define the derived global sections R\Gamma(X,-):=Rp_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(A), the derived direct image of [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]; it is represented by \Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet) for any K-injective resolution K\to\mathcal I^\bullet. For P,Q\in D(\mathcal O_X), define the global derived Hom complex $$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,Q):=R\Gamma\bigl(X,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(P,Q)\bigr)\in D(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)),$$ with R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X} the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. It is functorial in P (contravariantly) and Q (covariantly); when X=\operatorname{Spec}(R) it is an object of D(R), and after forgetting the A-module structure it is an object of the derived category of abelian groups.

proof.text: Use lem-pc-point-module-evaluation-equivalence for the pushforward ringed space globalSectionsPoint X. Its carrier is PUnit, so it has a Unique instance. Evaluation is an equivalence G; take G.asEquivalence, whose forward functor is G.

Let F be moduleDirectImage(toGlobalSectionsPoint X). The structure-ring map of this morphism is the identity and the inverse image of the whole point is X, so F followed by point evaluation G is naturally isomorphic to globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace. Both components are the identity linear map; naturality is reflexivity. Apply the existing library exact-postcomposition isomorphism Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso F G, then rightDerivedFunctorNatIso of this underived comparison. This gives RF followed by G.mapDerivedCategory isomorphic to schemeDerivedGlobalSections X, proving the point comparison.

For a quasi-isomorphism s:K -> I with I K-injective, Q.map s is an isomorphism. Apply schemeDerivedGlobalSections X to asIso(Q.map s), and compose with the existing library Functor.rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso for globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace at I. This proves the resolution computation. Global derived Hom remains the composite of internal derived Hom with the same global-sections derived functor.
